question: What was India's literacy rate at the time of independence in 1947?
solution:
The correct answer is __**12%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When the **British rule** ended in India in the year **1947**, the literacy rate was just around **12%**.
 
• The British rule in India refers to the period during which the Indian Subcontinent was under the colonial rule of the British Empire.
 
• It began in **1757**, following the** Battle of Plassey**, and continued until India gained independence on **August 15, 1947**.
 
• The British East India Company initially established a strong presence in India for trade, but over time, they gradually expanded their control over various **regions** and **Territories**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• According to the **2011 Census of India**, the overall rate of literacy is **73 percent**. But breaking up the national average reveals that while the rate of literacy for men is **80.9 **percent, for women it is** 65.46 percent**. This means that more than one-fourth of the country's population is still illiterate.
 
• Literacy forms an important input in the overall development of individuals enabling them to comprehend their social, political, and cultural environment better and respond to it appropriately.
 
• Higher levels of education and literacy lead to greater awareness and also contribute to the improvement of economic and social conditions.
 
• It acts as a catalyst for social upliftment enhancing the returns on investment made in almost every aspect of development effort, be it population control, health, hygiene, environmental degradation control, or employment of weaker sections of the society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The following are some of the important factors that could affect the low literacy rate of women in India-** 

 
 
• Poor school environment for girls 
 
• The lower enrolment 
 
• Dowry system 
 
• Early marriage
 
• Priority to the son’s education compared to the daughter’s education 
 
• Poverty
